title: Team AI Maturity Assessment
notes: Initial extracted config from the original static assessment implementation.
Scoring uses an evidence-weighted raw score normalized to 100 for display.
Question IDs and section IDs are stable handles for future backend storage and score comparability.

scoring.comparability: Scores from assessment-v01-rev-20260512a and later use weighted raw scoring normalized to 100. Store rawScore, rawMaxScore, revisionId, and question-level answers for cross-revision interpretation.

weighting.2: Stronger evidence signal: documented, repeatable, reviewable, or maintained behavior.

levels.name: Scattered
levels.description: Ad hoc AI use with isolated results. Context exists in individual chats and drives. No shared standards or reuse.
levels.tip: Focus on creating one shared context file and saving your best prompts.

levels.name: Structured
levels.description: Some repeatable practices but inconsistent. Context is scattered, handoffs vary, and reusable knowledge lives in individual tools.
levels.tip: Keep building foundations — standardize your handoffs and prompt library.

levels.name: Coordinated
levels.description: Aligned team practices and shared context. Your team works together with AI — the foundation is solid.
levels.tip: You're ready for governance and continuous improvement loops.

levels.name: Compounding
levels.description: Systematic advantage and continuous lift. AI is deeply embedded in your team's operating rhythm.
levels.tip: You're at the frontier — share what's working with peers.

sections.name: Shared Context
sections.description: How well your team creates and maintains shared AI context.

areaDescriptions.medium: Context exists but coverage is uneven.

questions.text: Our team has a shared document or file that describes our mission, goals, and key decisions that AI should always know.
When a new team member joins, they can quickly get AI tools up to speed on our work without asking everyone for context.
Team members use consistent background context when prompting AI tools—not whatever they happen to remember.
When our team's priorities or decisions change, we update our shared AI context files to reflect this.
Our AI context doesn't live in one person's head—it's documented and findable by anyone on the team.

sections.name: Prompt Reuse
sections.description: How well your team creates, stores, and reuses high-value prompts.

questions.text: We have a shared prompt library where team members store and find reusable prompts.
High-value prompts are not trapped in private chats—they're saved somewhere the team can access.
Our prompts include expected inputs, outputs, and instructions so others can use them without guessing.
Prompts are grouped by workflow, role, or task so people can find what they need quickly.
We regularly reuse and adapt prompts that worked well instead of starting from scratch.

sections.name: Team Handoffs
sections.description: How well context is preserved when work moves between people.

questions.text: When work moves from one team member to another, there's a standard format for summarizing AI context and decisions.
Handoff notes include what was tried, what worked, and what the AI needs to know to continue the work.
People don't have to re-explain the same background context every time they start a new conversation with AI.
Our handoff process captures key decisions and assumptions, not just task status.
When a project is paused and restarted, the team can quickly reload context without losing progress.

sections.name: Knowledge Capture
sections.description: How consistently your team records decisions and domain knowledge.

questions.text: Valuable insights and decisions from AI-assisted work are captured somewhere durable—not just in chat history.
When the AI produces something exceptional, we document what prompt or approach led to that result.
Domain-specific knowledge (definitions, constraints, policies) is written down and accessible to AI tools.
We have a way to capture and tag decisions so they can be referenced later without asking the person who made them.
Knowledge doesn't disappear when someone leaves the team or goes on leave.

sections.name: Review & Governance
sections.description: How your team reviews AI outputs and maintains standards.

questions.text: We have a clear process for reviewing AI-generated outputs before they become official or are acted upon.
There is someone or a role responsible for maintaining the quality of our AI context and prompts.
We track when context files or prompts were last updated and flag ones that may be stale.
Our team has shared standards for what makes a good prompt or AI output in our specific context.
When AI produces something wrong or misleading, we have a way to capture that feedback and improve.

sections.name: Workflow Integration
sections.description: How deeply AI is integrated into your team's daily workflows.

areaDescriptions.high: AI is deeply embedded in workflows.
areaDescriptions.medium: AI used in key workflows, unevenly.
areaDescriptions.low: AI use is ad hoc and individual.

questions.text: AI tools are consistently used across the team—not just by a few enthusiasts.
Our AI usage is integrated into regular workflows rather than used ad hoc when someone remembers.
We have standard places in our process where AI context is checked or updated (e.g., sprint start, handoffs).
Team members feel confident using AI tools because they know the context is reliable and up to date.
Our AI workflows have improved over time as we've learned what works and what doesn't.
